facts.statement: Tanycolagreus was a coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic in what are now the US states of Wyoming, Utah, and Colorado.
facts.quote: Tanycolagreus is a genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian to Tithonian) of the U.S. states of Wyoming, Utah, and Colorado.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton of Tanycolagreus was uncovered in 1995 at the Bone Cabin Quarry West locality in Wyoming.
facts.quote: In 1995 Western Paleontological Laboratories, Inc. uncovered the partial skeleton of a small theropod at the Bone Cabin Quarry West locality, Albany County, Wyoming, from the Salt Wash Member of the Morrison Formation, dating to the Kimmeridgian-Tithonian.

facts.statement: The genus Tanycolagreus was formally named and described by Kenneth Carpenter, Clifford Miles, and Karen Cloward in 2005.
facts.quote: It was actually named and described by Kenneth Carpenter, Clifford Miles and Karen Cloward in 2005.

facts.statement: The name Tanycolagreus means 'long-limbed hunter' and was chosen because its forelimbs and hindlimbs are longer than those of Coelurus.
facts.quote: The etymology of the generic name Tanycolagreus, suggested by Ben Creisler, is based upon the greater length of its forelimbs and hindlimbs compared to Coelurus.

facts.statement: The species name topwilsoni honors George Eugene "Top" Wilson, the father of a benefactor who supported the research.
facts.quote: The specific name honors George Eugene "Top" Wilson, the father of a benefactor financially supporting the scientific research.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton includes an incomplete skull, lower jaws, and much of the body skeleton behind the head.
facts.quote: It includes an incomplete skull and mandible (lower jaws) and much of the postcranial skeleton, i.e. the parts behind the head.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Tanycolagreus represents a subadult individual that was approximately 3.3 meters long.
facts.quote: Carpenter et al. (2005, pp. 43–44) determined that the holotype of Tanycolagreus represents a subadult individual which measured approximately 3.3 m long in life.

facts.statement: A referred fossil from the Cleveland-Lloyd Quarry suggests that some individuals of Tanycolagreus could reach a length of 4 meters.
facts.quote: However, one of the referred fossils, the premaxilla from the Cleveland-Lloyd Quarry, would have belonged to a larger individual, measuring 4 m long.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated that a four-meter-long Tanycolagreus would weigh approximately 120 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010 Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of a four-meter-long animal at 120 kg.

facts.statement: Tanycolagreus had a large, elongated head with a rectangular profile and a blunt snout.
facts.quote: The head of Tanycolagreus is large, elongated and rectangular in profile due to a blunt snout.

facts.statement: Tanycolagreus possessed long legs that were lightly built.
facts.quote: The leg is rather long and lightly built.

facts.statement: The second toe of Tanycolagreus was slightly hyperextendable but lacked an enlarged claw.
facts.quote: In the foot the second toe is slightly hyperextendable but does not carry an enlarged claw.

facts.statement: A 2007 phylogenetic analysis placed Tanycolagreus in a basal position within the Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: A detailed phylogenetic analysis in 2007 by Philip Senter including Tanycolagreus showed it had a basal position in the Tyrannosauroidea.

facts.statement: Later analyses suggested that Tanycolagreus held a basal position within the Coelurosauria.
facts.quote: Later analyses indicated a basal position in the Coelurosauria.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Tanycolagreus belongs to the Proceratosauridae; some 2025 analyses tentatively include it there, while others place it near but outside that family.
facts.quote: In their 2025 revision of the enigmatic Brazilian coelurosaurians Mirischia and Santanaraptor, Delcourt et al. consistently supported a Proceratosauridae clade. In equal-weight phylogenetic analyses, this group also tentatively included Tanycolagreus. However, in implied-weight phylogenetic analyses Tanycolagreus grouped with Mirischia, Santanaraptor and Juratyrant close to but not within Proceratosauridae.

facts.statement: Tanycolagreus lived approximately 152 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic in North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 152 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The species was initially thought to be Coelurus but was announced as a new species named Tanycolagreus topwilsoni in 2001.
facts.quote: Al principio, se consideró que el hallazgo era un espécimen de Coelurus, pero un estudio posterior indicó que representaba una especie nueva para la ciencia, que en 2001 se anunció que se llamaría Tanycolagreus topwilsoni.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil, TPII 2000-09-29, was donated to science by an anonymous benefactor.
facts.quote: El fósil, holotipo TPII 2000-09-29, fue donado a la ciencia por un benefactor anónimo.

facts.statement: Fossils of Tanycolagreus come from the Morrison Formation, dated to the Oxfordian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: en la Formación Morrison datada de Oxfordiense al Titoniense.

facts.statement: Remains possibly referred to Stokesosaurus have been recovered from stratigraphic zone 5 of the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Se han recuperado restos posiblemente referidos a Stokesosaurus de la zona estratigráfica 5 de la Formación Morrison.

facts.statement: The skull is less well known than the postcranial skeleton, with only specific elements like the left nasal, right lacrimal, and various jaw bones found.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Tanycolagreus es menos conocido que su esqueleto postcraneal y solamente se han encontrado los siguientes elementos: nasal izquierdo, lacrimal derecho, diente premaxilar derecho y un premaxilar, postorbital derecho, cuadradoyugal, el hueso escamoso izquierdo incompleto, dientes del hueso cuadrado derecho en la zona articular y malar, espleniales derecho e izquierdo.

facts.statement: The genus name Tanycolagreus refers to its long forelimbs and honors George "Top" Wilson, the namesake of the species.
facts.quote: La etimología de Tanycolagreus se basa en la estructura de sus miembros delanteros largos, del griego clásico tany largo, estirado kolon miembro y agreus cazador, el nombre de la especie se da por George "Top" Wilson.

facts.statement: A paratype specimen, AMNH 587, consists of an incomplete hand originally collected from Bone Cabin Quarry and referred to Ornitholestes hermanni in 1903.
facts.quote: Se ha asignado un paratipo a la especie, el espécimen AMNH 587, que consiste en una mano incompleta también recolectada de Bone Cabin Quarry y originalmente en 1903 por Henry Fairfield Osborn referido a Ornitholestes hermanni.

facts.statement: Carpenter and colleagues originally assigned Tanycolagreus to the family Coeluridae.
facts.quote: Carpenter y colegas originalmente asignaron a Tanycolagreus a Coeluridae.

facts.statement: A detailed phylogenetic analysis by Philip Senter in 2007 showed that Tanycolagreus had a basal position within Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético detallado realizado en 2007 por Philip Senter, incluido Tanycolagreus, mostró que tenía una posición basal en Tyrannosauroidea.

facts.statement: Subsequent analyses indicated a basal position for Tanycolagreus within Coelurosauria.
facts.quote: Análisis posteriores indicaron una posición basal en Coelurosauria.

facts.statement: Tanycolagreus belongs to the parent group Coelurosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coelurosauria

facts.statement: Tanycolagreus lived between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago, during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tanycolagreus fossils are present in stratigraphic zone 2 of the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Tanycolagreus está presente en la zona estratigráfica 2 de Morrison.
